cards.front: Secondary PPH (24 hours to 6 weeks postpartum) is most commonly due to retained products of conception or [___]; investigate with pelvic ultrasound.
cards.context:
Retained placental tissue and endometritis (infection of the uterine lining) can prevent normal uterine involution, causing bleeding 24 hours to 6 weeks after birth.

Fever, uterine tenderness and offensive lochia support endometritis. Assess blood loss and haemodynamic status first; check a full blood count.

Pelvic ultrasound helps assess retained tissue, but normal postpartum appearances can be misleading. If infection is suspected, take indicated cultures and start broad-spectrum antibiotics without waiting for results.

cards.front: A low-risk woman has a newly abnormal fetal heart rate on intermittent auscultation. Begin further assessment with [___].
cards.context:
An abnormal fetal heart rate detected by intermittent auscultation needs cardiotocography for further assessment.

Interpret the trace with the clinical history and risk factors rather than treating one number as a diagnosis.

cards.front: A woman with two previous miscarriages attends an early pregnancy clinic with bleeding and a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy. Which vaginal medication should be recommended until 16 weeks? [___]
cards.context:
Progesterone should be recommended when there is early pregnancy bleeding and two or more previous miscarriages. It probably increases the live birth rate.

Give micronised progesterone vaginally, 400 mg twice daily, and continue to 16 weeks.

reference.title: Miscarriage, Recurrent Miscarriage and Ectopic Pregnancy (C-Gyn 38)

cards.front: ECV is offered from 36-37 weeks for breech presentation; success rate is approximately [___]%.
cards.context:
ECV = manual rotation of breech baby to cephalic by abdominal manipulation, done at 36-37 weeks (earlier baby may turn back; later uterus too tight + fluid too low).

Success ~50% overall, ~70% with multiparity/posterior placenta/adequate liquor/non-engaged breech/operator experience. Contraindications: placenta praevia, APH, ruptured membranes, abnormal CTG, multiple pregnancy.

Tocolysis (terbutaline 250 µg subcut) improves success; monitor CTG before/during/30-60 min after; if ECV fails → planned CS at 39 weeks.

cards.front: The increased tendency to clot after childbirth is called a [___] state.
cards.context:
Delivery-related tissue injury, venous stasis and persistent hypercoagulability raise postpartum clot risk, especially in the first six weeks. A smaller excess risk can persist beyond six weeks.

Prophylaxis depends on individual risk assessment. Australian guidance distinguishes prophylaxis until discharge, at least seven days and six weeks; Caesarean birth alone does not mandate six weeks.

cards.front: At 33 weeks, a woman develops nocturnal itching of her palms and soles without a primary rash. Non-fasting bile acids are 28 µmol/L (pregnancy reference <19); transaminases are normal. Other hepatic disease is excluded. The diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
Bile acids establish the biochemical abnormality; normal transaminases do not exclude this pregnancy disorder.

A primary inflammatory rash would favour a dermatosis. Scratch marks alone are compatible with cholestasis.

cards.front: Lactation hormones: [___] (anterior pituitary) drives milk production; oxytocin (posterior pituitary) triggers let-down. The latter is inhibited by stress and pain.
cards.context:
Lactation runs on two complementary hormones. Prolactin (anterior pituitary) drives MILK PRODUCTION, rising with each suckling stimulus and peaking at night.

Oxytocin (posterior pituitary) drives the LET-DOWN reflex, contracting myoepithelial cells to eject stored milk.

Oxytocin release is conditioned to multiple cues but exquisitely sensitive to stress, pain, alcohol, embarrassment — these inhibit let-down even when supply is fine.

cards.front: Australian cervical screening (since Dec 2017): [___] testing every 5 years from ages 25-74, with reflex cytology if positive. Type 16/18 → straight to colposcopy.
cards.context:
Australian Cervical Screening changed Dec 2017 from 2-yearly Pap (cytology-first) to 5-yearly HPV (HPV-first) with reflex LBC only if HPV positive — HPV testing has higher sensitivity for precancerous lesions.

Pathway: HPV positive + 16/18 → colposcopy; HPV positive other types → reflex cytology (abnormal → colposcopy, normal → repeat in 12 months); HPV negative → routine 5-yearly.

cards.front: The less variable ovarian phase is the luteal phase, which usually lasts about [___] days.
cards.context:
The luteal phase is less variable than the follicular phase and is usually about 12-14 days, but a normal range of roughly 11-17 days is recognised; it is not fixed at exactly 14 days.

Practically, subtracting 14 days from the next expected period gives an estimate of ovulation, not an exact date for every cycle. The mid-cycle rule only fits a textbook 28-day cycle.

Counting back from the next expected period is more accurate for fertility timing, ovulation detection, and luteal phase assessment in subfertility workup.

cards.front: A dating scan, when done, is recommended at 8-14 weeks; it confirms [___], dates the pregnancy, and detects multiple gestation.
cards.context:
Australian guidance recommends a dating scan, when done, between 8+0 and 13+6 weeks. It confirms viability, dates pregnancy by CRL, and identifies multiple pregnancy/chorionicity.

Book it in this narrow window because CRL dating is more accurate than later biparietal diameter/head circumference estimates, and chorionicity is easiest to assess while membranes are clearly visible.

cards.front: Prior spontaneous preterm birth <34 weeks PLUS current cervical length ≤25 mm: offer vaginal [___] and/or cervical cerclage.
cards.context:
Prior spontaneous preterm birth + current short cervix is the highest-risk group; both interventions can be offered. Vaginal progesterone (200 mg pessary nightly, 16-24 wk until 34-36 wk) cuts preterm birth ~40%.

Cervical cerclage (McDonald suture at 12-14 weeks) is offered for history-indicated (≥3 prior preterm births/losses) or USS-indicated (CL <25 mm with prior preterm birth) cases.

The Arabin pessary is a non-surgical alternative — evidence mixed.

cards.front: Vasa praevia is diagnosed with transvaginal USS plus [___], confirming unprotected fetal vessels crossing or lying near the internal cervical os.
cards.context:
Transvaginal colour Doppler confirms fetal-rate pulsatile flow in unprotected vessels crossing or lying near the internal cervical os, distinguishing them from a free cord loop or maternal vessel.

Do not use 2 cm as a supposedly safe diagnostic boundary: it was extrapolated from placenta praevia, and safety for vaginal birth has not been demonstrated. Expert definitions vary, with some using a 5 cm radius.

Universal screening isn't recommended (too many false positives at prevalence ~1 in 2500). Screen high-risk pregnancies: velamentous cord insertion, succenturiate or bilobed placenta, low-lying placenta or praevia.

cards.front: For stress incontinence, first-line conservative management is supervised [___] for at least 3 months before reassessment.
cards.context:
PFMT is first-line conservative therapy for stress urinary incontinence; bladder training leads for pure urge/urgency incontinence, with PFMT as an adjunct.

In SUI, stronger levator ani support lifts the bladder neck and improves urethral closure during exertion.

Supervised PFMT needs at least 3 months for strength gains; 60-70% of women improve enough to avoid drug adverse effects or surgery.

cards.front: Safer Baby Bundle: settle to sleep on the side from [___] weeks, because going to sleep supine is linked to late stillbirth; lying supine compresses the IVC.
cards.context:
Going to sleep supine from 28 weeks is associated with late stillbirth (pooled adjusted odds ratio 2.63); either side appears equally safe.

Supine at 35-38 weeks, MRI shows IVC flow falls by about 85% and cardiac output by about 16% despite azygos collaterals: a plausible mechanism, not proven cause.

cards.front: NT >=[___] mm — a separate, fixed threshold above the >95th-centile aneuploidy-screening cutoff — is independently associated with structural anomalies including cardiac defects.
cards.context:
Increased NT (>95th centile for CRL, roughly 2.1-2.8 mm across the 11-14 week window) is a non-specific marker of fetal stress — fluid accumulation behind the fetal neck from any cause altering lymphatic drainage.

This is the aneuploidy-screening trigger. NT ≥3.5 mm is a separate, higher, fixed cutoff independently associated with cardiac and other structural anomalies, regardless of the aneuploidy screening result.

Picks up aneuploidies (T21, T18, T13, monosomy X), structural anomalies (cardiac, diaphragmatic hernia), and genetic syndromes with normal karyotype.

cards.front: Normal cardiotocograph (CTG): baseline [___] bpm, variability 6-25 bpm, accelerations present, no decelerations.
cards.context:
Normal CTG has four reassuring features: baseline 110-160 bpm (bradycardia <110 may be cord/heart block, tachycardia >160 may be sepsis/hypoxia).

DR C BRAVADO structures interpretation: Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline Rate, Variability, Accelerations, Decelerations, Overall.

cards.front: The 4 Ts of PPH causes: Tone (atony, ~70%), Trauma (lacerations, ~20%), [___] (retained, ~10%), and Thrombin.
cards.context:
4 Ts mnemonic ranks PPH causes by frequency: Tone (atony, ~70% — uterus fails to contract); Trauma (~20% — perineal/vaginal/cervical lacerations); Tissue (~10% — retained placenta or products)

Thrombin (~1% — coagulopathy). PPH = ≥500 mL after vaginal delivery or ≥1000 mL after CS. Surgical: B-Lynch, uterine artery ligation/embolisation, hysterectomy as last resort.

cards.front: [___] is the most common cause of postpartum haemorrhage, accounting for 70-80% of cases.
cards.context:
Risk factors include: prolonged labour, overdistended uterus (multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, macrosomia), chorioamnionitis, grand multiparity, and uterine relaxants (MgSO₄, volatile anaesthetics).

The uterus should be palpated after every delivery — a boggy, poorly contracted uterus requires immediate action.

cards.front: First-line manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia is McRoberts position with [___] pressure (NOT fundal); resolves majority of cases.
cards.context:
The mechanism: hyperflexing the maternal hips onto the abdomen rotates the symphysis pubis cephalad and flattens the sacral promontory, straightening the pelvic axis and increasing the AP diameter by 1-2 cm.

Suprapubic (NOT fundal) pressure adds adduction of the anterior shoulder into the oblique diameter.

McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure resolves around 60-90% of shoulder dystocia cases — making it the highest-yield first-line manoeuvre.

cards.front: Bacterial vaginosis is a polymicrobial dysbiosis (Gardnerella, Mobiluncus, Atopobium replacing the [___]-dominated normal flora). It recurs in 30-50% of women within 3 months — the 2025 StepUp RCT found concurrent male-partner treatment reduces recurrence in heterosexual couples.
cards.context:
BV is anaerobic dysbiosis: Gardnerella, Mobiluncus and Atopobium overgrow as Lactobacillus-dominated flora is lost.

Recurrence is common. The 2025 StepUp RCT found concurrent male-partner metronidazole plus topical clindamycin reduced 12-week recurrence in heterosexual couples.
